condition: Endoscopy antithrombotic management — warfarin continued for diagnostic OGD ± biopsy
summary: 74-year-old woman on warfarin for AF (INR 2.3) booked for diagnostic gastroscopy ± biopsy for PPI-refractory dyspepsia (low bleeding-risk procedure).

inputs.chiefComplaint: Booked for a camera test of the stomach — takes warfarin
inputs.hpi: Three months of upper abdominal discomfort and reflux not settling on omeprazole. No weight loss, dysphagia, vomiting or melaena. Booked for diagnostic gastroscopy ± biopsies. Atrial fibrillation on warfarin (target 2–3), no previous stroke, no valve disease.

exam.general: Well. Irregular pulse 76, BP 132/78, RR 14, SpO2 97% on air, T 36.5°C.
exam.abdomen: Soft, mild epigastric tenderness, no mass.

mustExclude.note: Low-risk procedure: warfarin continued; bridging is both unnecessary and a bleeding risk.
Reversing a therapeutic INR for a diagnostic gastroscopy exposes the patient to thromboembolism for no benefit.

guideline.name: BSG/ESGE guideline — endoscopy in patients on antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy (2021 update)
guideline.section: Low-risk procedures (diagnostic ± biopsy): continue P2Y12 inhibitors and warfarin (INR in the week before, within therapeutic range), omit the morning DOAC dose. High-risk procedures (polypectomy, EMR, ERCP with sphincterotomy): P2Y12 inhibitor stopped 7 days before when thrombotic risk is low; high thrombotic risk (coronary stents) — continue aspirin and liaise with the cardiologist about stopping the P2Y12 inhibitor; warfarin stopped 5 days before (INR <1.5), bridging only for high thrombotic risk; DOAC stopped before the procedure (interval by drug and renal function), no bridging
guideline.citation: Veitch AM, Radaelli F, Alikhan R, et al. Gut. 2021;70:1611–28.

guideline.name: BRIDGE trial — perioperative bridging anticoagulation in AF
guideline.section: Forgoing bridging was non-inferior for arterial thromboembolism and reduced major bleeding in patients with AF interrupting warfarin
guideline.citation: Douketis JD, Spyropoulos AC, Kaatz S, et al. N Engl J Med. 2015;373:823–33.

rationale: Permutation: low bleeding-risk procedure on warfarin. The right answer is to continue warfarin (INR within range). Tests over-management: bridging, reversal or deferral.
